En la parte anterior del pecho. El pecto: At the front of the chest. The pectoralis major runs from the collarbone and breastbone towards the upper arm bone, the humerus.
Pectoral mayor: la capa amplia y superfi: Pectoralis major: the broad, superficial layer of the chest.
Pectoral menor: una capa más profunda qu: Pectoralis minor: a deeper layer connecting ribs and shoulder blade.
Hombro: el mayor acerca el brazo al cuer: Shoulder: the major brings the arm towards the body and across the chest. The minor acts on the shoulder blade, rather than the elbow.
En un empuje, el pecho participa en el h: In a push, the chest contributes at the shoulder and the triceps straightens the elbow. The anterior deltoid and the muscles positioning the shoulder blade also take part.
En una flexión, seguí el brazo desde el: In a push-up, follow the arm from the shoulder, then look at the elbow: these are two different joints within the same push.
Rodean el hombro como una capa sobre la: They cover the shoulder like a layer over the upper humerus. They connect to the collarbone and shoulder blade.
Porción anterior: delante del hombro; ay: Anterior portion: at the front of the shoulder; helps bring the arm forwards.
Porción media: a un lado; ayuda a separa: Middle portion: at the side; helps move the arm away from the body.
Porción posterior: detrás; ayuda a lleva: Posterior portion: at the back; helps bring the arm backwards.
Hombro: levantar el brazo hacia adelante: Shoulder: raising the arm forwards, sideways or backwards depending on the portion involved. The deltoid is not the only muscle moving this joint.
La escápula aporta la base móvil del hom: The shoulder blade provides a moving base for the shoulder. The rotator cuff, a deep group distinct from the deltoid, also helps control the joint.
En el modelo, girá desde la vista fronta: In the model, rotate from the front view to the back and locate the three sides of the shoulder before following an arm raise.
En la cara posterior del brazo, entre el: At the back of the upper arm, between the shoulder and elbow. Its tendon reaches the olecranon, the bony tip of the elbow.
Cabeza larga: comienza en la escápula y: Long head: starts at the shoulder blade and also crosses the shoulder.
Cabezas lateral y medial: comienzan en e: Lateral and medial heads: start at the humerus; all three join the same tendon.
Codo: aumentar su ángulo para estirar el: Elbow: increasing its angle to straighten the arm. The long head also crosses the shoulder; the other two do not.
En una flexión, el tríceps participa en: In a push-up, the triceps contributes at the elbow while the chest and shoulder act higher up. Straightening the elbow and moving the arm from the shoulder are different tasks.
Pausá una flexión con el codo doblado y: Pause a push-up with the elbow bent and compare it with the straighter arm. Look for the change at the elbow, not just how far the body rises.
El dorsal ancho cubre buena parte de la: The latissimus dorsi covers much of the lower and outer back; it narrows towards the armpit and attaches to the humerus.
Dorsal ancho derecho e izquierdo: múscul: Right and left latissimus dorsi: broad muscles connecting the trunk to the arm.
Hombro: acercar el brazo al tronco y lle: Shoulder: bringing the arm towards the trunk and backwards. The lat moves the arm; it does not directly bend the elbow.
En un remo, el dorsal participa en el ho: In a row, the lat contributes at the shoulder, the elbow flexors bend the arm and the scapular muscles accompany the position of the shoulder blade.
En un remo, seguí el codo cuando se acer: In a row, follow the elbow as it approaches the trunk and also look at the shoulder. Bending the elbow is only one part of the pulling movement.
En la cara anterior del brazo. Sus dos c: At the front of the upper arm. Its two heads start at the shoulder blade and its tendon reaches the radius, one of the forearm bones.
Cabeza larga y cabeza corta: dos puntos: Long and short heads: two origins forming the biceps brachii.
Codo: doblarlo. Antebrazo: girarlo para: Elbow: bending it. Forearm: turning it to face the palm upwards, called supination. It also crosses the shoulder and helps bring the arm forwards.
El braquial y el braquiorradial también: The brachialis and brachioradialis also bend the elbow. Bending the arm therefore does not show that only the biceps is working.
Compará doblar el codo con girar el ante: Compare bending the elbow with rotating the forearm: you can change the direction of the palm without completing another elbow bend.
Detrás del cuello y del tórax. El trapec: Behind the neck and ribcage. The trapezius extends towards the collarbone and shoulder blade; the deeper rhomboids lie between the spine and the inner edge of the shoulder blade.
Trapecio: porciones superior, media e in: Trapezius: upper, middle and lower portions with different orientations.
Romboides mayor y menor: unen la columna: Rhomboid major and minor: connect the spine to the shoulder blade.
Cintura escapular: elevar, bajar y acerc: Shoulder girdle: raising, lowering and bringing the shoulder blades towards the spine, with different roles depending on the muscle. The shoulder blade moves over the ribcage; it is not a hinge like the elbow.
Estos músculos comparten el control esca: These muscles share shoulder blade control with the serratus anterior and other shoulder muscles. Positioning the shoulder blade provides a base for arm movement.
En una W en el suelo, mirá la relación e: In a floor W raise, look at the relationship between shoulder blades, ribs and arms. Then compare it with a row: controlling the shoulder blade and pulling against a load are different tasks.
Entre las costillas y la pelvis. El rect: Between the ribs and pelvis. The rectus abdominis lies at the front, on each side of the midline; the transverse abdominis forms a deep layer around the abdomen.
Recto abdominal: bandas largas que ayuda: Rectus abdominis: long bands that help bend the trunk.
Transverso abdominal: fibras transversal: Transverse abdominis: transverse fibres that compress the abdominal wall.
Columna y pelvis: el recto ayuda a acerc: Spine and pelvis: the rectus helps bring the ribcage towards the pelvis. The transverse abdominis compresses the abdomen; its work does not require a large visible bend.
La pared abdominal trabaja con los oblic: The abdominal wall works with the obliques and back muscles to move or control the trunk. The muscles moving the arms and legs have other tasks.
Al incorporarte para salir de la cama, e: As you sit up to get out of bed, the trunk changes position while the arms and hips can also help.
En un dead bug, seguí la distancia entre: In a dead bug, follow the distance between ribs and pelvis as the limbs move. The cue is what the trunk maintains, not just what moves.
A los lados del abdomen, entre costillas: At the sides of the abdomen, between ribs and pelvis. The external oblique is more superficial and the internal oblique lies underneath.
Oblicuo externo: capa superficial con fi: External oblique: a superficial layer with diagonal fibres.
Oblicuo interno: capa más profunda con o: Internal oblique: a deeper layer with a different orientation; both are present on the right and left.
Columna: girar e inclinar el tronco. Al: Spine: rotating and bending the trunk sideways. Together they also help bend it forwards and compress the abdomen; the combination of sides changes the movement.
Cooperan con recto, transverso y músculo: They work with the rectus abdominis, transverse abdominis and back muscles. They can accompany rotation or help control a posture when a load pulls to one side.
En los toques de hombro en plancha, mirá: In plank shoulder taps, look for rotation of the pelvis and ribcage when one hand leaves the floor. The change in support helps explain the work of control.
En la parte posterior y lateral de la ca: At the back and side of the hip. The gluteus maximus is more superficial; the medius and minimus lie towards the side of the pelvis, in deeper layers.
Glúteo mayor: destaca en llevar el muslo: Gluteus maximus: especially involved in bringing the thigh backwards, extending the hip.
Glúteos medio y menor: forman parte del: Gluteus medius and minimus: part of the lateral group that moves and supports the hip.
Cadera: extenderla, separar el muslo del: Hip: extending it, moving the thigh away from the body and controlling its position, with different roles within the group. Extending the hip is different from arching the back.
Al levantarte de una silla, cadera y rod: When getting up from a chair, the hips and knees extend together. Glutes, thigh muscles and trunk work together; one group does not explain the whole movement.
En un puente, seguí cómo cambia la relac: In a bridge, follow the changing relationship between pelvis and thighs. Compare that hip movement with the position of the trunk.
En la parte anterior y a los lados del m: At the front and sides of the thigh. All four muscles reach the kneecap and transmit force towards the tibia through the knee’s tendon mechanism.
Recto femoral: delante del muslo; cruza: Rectus femoris: at the front of the thigh; crosses the hip and knee.
Vastos lateral, medial e intermedio: rod: Vastus lateralis, medialis and intermedius: surround the femur; the intermedius lies beneath the rectus femoris.
Rodilla: extenderla, pasando de doblada: Knee: extending it, from bent to straighter. The rectus femoris also helps bend the hip; the three vasti act on the knee.
En una sentadilla, el cuádriceps partici: In a squat, the quadriceps contributes at the knee and the hip muscles act higher up. Foot support and trunk control are also part of the movement.
En una sentadilla, seguí el ángulo de la: In a squat, follow the angle of the knee as you lower and rise. Then look at the hip: a squat combines both joints.
En la parte posterior del muslo. La mayo: At the back of the thigh. Most of the group connects the pelvis to the lower leg, crossing the hip and knee.
Bíceps femoral: cabezas larga y corta en: Biceps femoris: long and short heads on the outer side of the thigh.
Semitendinoso y semimembranoso: hacia el: Semitendinosus and semimembranosus: towards the inner side.
Rodilla: flexionarla. Cadera: ayudar a e: Knee: bending it. Hip: helping extend it. The short head of the biceps femoris crosses only the knee; it does not directly extend the hip.
Cooperan con los glúteos en gestos de ex: They work with the glutes in hip extension. At the knee, their action differs from the quadriceps’ extension; these tasks combine according to the movement.
En una bisagra de cadera, mirá cuánto ca: In a hip hinge, look at how much the hip changes and how much the knee changes. Compare it with bringing the heel backwards to distinguish the group’s two actions.
En la parte posterior de la pierna, deba: At the back of the lower leg, below the knee. The gastrocnemius and soleus reach the heel through the calcaneal tendon, known as the Achilles tendon.
Gastrocnemio o gemelos: dos cabezas supe: Gastrocnemius: two superficial heads; crosses the knee and ankle.
Sóleo: capa más profunda; cruza el tobil: Soleus: a deeper layer; crosses the ankle but not the knee.
Tobillo: apuntar el pie hacia abajo, lla: Ankle: pointing the foot downwards, called plantar flexion; with the foot supported, this is visible as the heel rises. The gastrocnemius also helps bend the knee.
La elevación del talón combina pantorril: A heel raise combines the calf, foot support and balance. Other lower leg and foot muscles help orient and maintain the support.
En una elevación de talones, ubicá el to: In a heel raise, locate the ankle and follow the heel as it leaves the floor. This is different from straightening the knee.
